title: docs(adr): ADR-0066 unified authorization model
body:
Consolidates ObjectStack's authorization layers and fills four gaps surfaced by the `sys_license` case (a platform-global, super-admin-only, secret-bearing control object that the current model couldn't express cleanly).

### Three-way separation (principle)
- **Capability** — *what can be done* (defined by platform/package).
- **Assignment** — *who holds it* — permission sets / roles / bindings (**admin-maintained runtime records, [existing]**).
- **Requirement** — *what a resource needs* — the resource **references** a capability (a contract, **not** an assignment).

### Four additions (each reuses existing vocabulary; all tagged [existing]/[new])
- **D1 capability registry** — capabilities become first-class records (not bare strings); admins/packages add new ones; existing strings seeded for back-compat.
- **D2 secure-by-default posture** — an object/field can opt out of the allow-by-default wildcard grant (`access:{default:'private'}`), like Salesforce "new object = no access until granted". A data-model posture (like `tenancy`), names no principal.
- **D3 resource→capability requirement** — extend `requiredPermissions` (today only on App) to Object/Field/Action.
- **D4 dual-surface action gates** — one declaration gates both the UI (ActionRunner) and the server.
- **D5 package-seeded, admin-maintainable policies** — a package locks its sensitive objects on install; admins tune in Setup.

### Kept (existing strengths)
Permission sets/roles/bindings (assignment), full RLS spectrum (ownership/hierarchy ADR-0057/tenant/sharing/CEL), `tenancy`, `App.requiredPermissions`, anti-escalation, union grants.

`sys_license` worked example included. Open-core: mechanism in framework; policies are data. Phased (D2+D3 object first — the minimal unblock).
